scope: Six independent headless straight probes at x=6,y=0,yaw=0; same 550kg/1200 damping/300 mount, aligned stationary capture enable, stamped body commands, unchanged 0.8 m/s² controller acceleration, 10km/h cruise, braking to HOLD. Same OptiX visual road; only road collision representation differs.
contact_velocity_definition: Native GZ wheel world linear velocity + angular velocity cross (contact point - wheel link origin), projected tangent to contact normal. Other collision must belong to a static road model. This is the primary mechanical slip evidence.
limitations: Small-angle height*pitch estimate is explanatory, not an exact terrain/rolling reconstruction.
Absolute tangent travel covers observed contact samples only; no-contact gaps are reported separately.
This is a startup diagnostic, not full-area repeat acceptance or a real-tyre validation.
conclusion: All six matched startup probes reproduce encoder/body/camera travel discrepancies while native contact tangent speeds remain small. First-second encoder/body difference 12.14-12.38 mm is mostly explained by the pitching reference frame (12.47-12.71 mm small-angle estimate; remainder about -0.31 to -0.32 mm). Neither representation exhibits the substantial wheel-ground sliding implied by interpreting the camera ratio as tyre slip. This does not retrospectively prove all old full-run intervals slip-free.
encoder_distance_definition: Integral of archived fl shaft peripheral speed using the plugin nominal radius; continuous kinematic diagnostic, not a recount of AB edges or emitted image rows.
